headline: Shared git/project writes make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors medium-risk; no critical compliance mismatch is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and shares state via a git repo, while gpt-engineer writes files in a project directory and then offers to run them. That creates a default file-based bridge where one agent can ingest the other's generated content as trusted instructions. No MCP or clipboard bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or project directory, file content can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent treats generated files as instructions without provenance checks, injected text can steer subsequent actions.
mitigations: Use separate directories for the two agents.
Add a human review step before either agent consumes the other's output.
Prefix generated artifacts with machine-readable provenance markers.
Disable automatic execution of newly written files.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing or allowlists.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and read/write filesystem access, and both touch code in shared working trees. If sensitive source or secrets are present in the shared workspace, either agent can transmit them to configured model providers. The profiles do not show local-only inference or isolation, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared workspace, either agent can read them.
IF either agent sends file contents to its configured model provider, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project tree.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Restrict network egress at the host or container level.
Rotate any secrets that were already stored in the repo.
requires-engineering: route both agents through a local inference endpoint.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can modify git state and write the shared repo, while gpt-engineer can write files in the project directory. They overlap on mutable filesystem state, but only Aider explicitly modifies git state, so the strongest high-severity git-lock conflict is not fully supported. The shared project/repo still creates a real write collision risk.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same files or directories concurrently, writes can overwrite each other.
IF Aider commits while gpt-engineer is mid-write, repository state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping file ownership.
Serialize edits with a simple manual turn-taking rule.
Commit or snapshot after each agent finishes.
Use separate branches for each agent.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run them, and Aider can modify code and git history. That makes Aider's output a likely input to gpt-engineer or vice versa, with no documented verification step between them. The pair can therefore propagate incorrect code or assumptions across multiple work products.
conditions: IF one agent's generated code is fed into the other without review, errors can cascade.
IF either agent executes or commits the other's output, mistakes become persistent.
mitigations: Insert a manual review gate between agents.
Require tests before accepting generated changes.
Limit each agent to a narrow task slice.
Compare outputs against a checklist before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated validation and diff-based approval.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with no explicit residency, HIPAA, or retention mismatch documented. The only compliance-relevant issue visible is that both may send prompts or file contents to configured model providers, but the profiles do not show a specific cross-border or certification conflict. One citation per agent is sufficient because this is a profile-only compatibility check, not an interaction pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's prompt or workspace, external model-provider processing may create a policy issue.
IF the deployment requires residency guarantees, the configured provider must satisfy them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of prompts and repos.
Use a provider approved for the relevant data class.
Document retention settings before use.
Review vendor terms for both tools.
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls in the orchestrator.
